title: Find the variance floor, then bag stumps and score them out of bag
brief: Evaluate the variance of an average and simulate correlated models, then draw bootstrap samples, bag stumps, and compute the out-of-bag error from the rows each stump never saw.
hints: bagging_variance is rho * sigma2 + (1 - rho) * sigma2 / B. With rho = 0.5, sigma2 = 4, B = 2 it is 3.
In correlated_estimators draw shared with rng.normal(size=(n_draws, 1)) and private with rng.normal(size=(n_draws, B)). Broadcasting gives every column in a row the same shared value.
trees_needed is ceil((1 - rho) / (tol * rho)), raised to at least 1. With rho = 0.3 and tol = 0.05 it is 47.
bootstrap_indices is one call: rng.integers(0, n, size=n). Every entry is an independent draw from 0 to n - 1, so repeats are expected.
In fit_bagged_stumps, draw idx once per estimator, fit _fit_stump(X[idx], y[idx]), and append both the stump and idx. The out-of-bag functions need idx to know which rows each stump missed.
bagged_predict stacks one prediction vector per stump into an array of shape (len(stumps), n), then averages down axis 0.
oob_mask starts from in_bag = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool), sets in_bag[idx] = True, and returns ~in_bag. A repeated index writes the same slot twice, so you do not need np.unique.

In oob_predictions keep total and count arrays of shape (n,). For each stump, add its predictions into total[mask] and add 1 into count[mask], where mask = oob_mask(idx, n). Divide only where count > 0 and put np.nan elsewhere.
In out_of_bag_error, average the squared error over the rows where count > 0, and raise ValueError when there are none. On the hand example the answer is 50.
